hypothesis: Customer discrimination partly depends on across-window location, dispersion, tails, and extremes discarded by single-vector pooling; fixed multi-statistic pooling over learned latent window representations may recover that information under customer-level supervision.

pooling.quantile_algorithm: torch.sort plus linear interpolation at q*(m-1)

training.initialization: Xavier uniform linear weights; zero biases

comparisons: mean latent-HGB probability minus FULL_48 HGB
mean latent-HGB probability minus direct-distribution HGB

outcomes.A: Mean latent-HGB deltas versus FULL_48 >= +0.010 ROC and +0.020 AP; at least 4/5 seeds improve both; both paired lower bounds > 0; gains over direct HGB >= +0.005 ROC and +0.010 AP with both lower bounds > 0.
outcomes.B: Mean latent-HGB deltas versus FULL_48 >= -0.005 ROC and -0.010 AP; at least 4/5 seeds within both margins; paired lower bounds exceed those margins; latent HGB non-worse than direct on both means and gains >= +0.005 ROC or +0.010 AP with corresponding lower bound > 0.
outcomes.C: Neither A nor B; material inferiority if mean ROC delta < -0.015 or mean AP delta < -0.030.

failure_policy: Outcome C ends the neural representation direction unless a qualitatively new external hypothesis is introduced.
